feedback.problem: The eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}k & -1 \\ 2 & 2k\end{aligned}]$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =k+2$ is  $[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ k-1\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =\lambda v \\ [\begin{aligned}k & -1 \\ 2 & 2k\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ k-1\end{aligned}] & =(k+2)[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ k-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2k+1 \\ -2+2{k}^{2}-2k\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-k-2 \\ {k}^{2}+k-2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2k+1=-k-2, \\ -2+2{k}^{2}-2k={k}^{2}+k-2\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $k$ in the first equation, we get

$$
-k=-3\,⟹\,k=3.
$$

Now, substituting $k=3$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2+2{k}^{2}-2k & ={k}^{2}+k-2 \\ -2+2\cdot (3)^{2}-2\cdot 3 & =(3)^{2}+3-2 \\ 10 & =10,\end{aligned}
$$

which is a true statement.

Therefore, the solution of the system is $k=3.$
